angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,169,472 km at 10.93 pc = 1.43 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 102870: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 91.5 +/- 0.22 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 10.929 +/- 0.026 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 90.8945 +/- 0.1934 mas (same row, RUWE 2.81), 470.0 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.681 +/- 0.008 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 102870: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.431 +/- 0.006 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.681 +/- 0.008 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 1,169,472 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.324 +/- 0.005 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 102870: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.324 +/- 0.005 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6132 +/- 26 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 102870: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6132 +/- 26 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 102870: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6132 +/- 26 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/zavijava.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.109, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
